entries.title: Pullback Continuation Dukascopy-Native Independent Alpha and Portfolio Portability Study
entries.target_failure_mode: Determine whether the fixed Pullback Continuation mechanism has executable and period-portable alpha when its event population and execution are defined entirely on one Dukascopy Bid/Ask Tick lineage.
entries.causal_hypothesis: A strong EMA-separated trend that retraces to EMA20 and completes a directional confirmation bar contains a 16-M15-bar continuation edge across 2023H1-2024H2 after source-native Bid/Ask execution.
pre_result_predictions: The source-native candidate should remain profitable with PF at least 1.10.
All four development folds should be positive and no fold should be negative.
At least 16 of 24 months should be positive.
Both directions remain eligible; no direction, session or period is removed after outcomes.
tests: 24-month Dukascopy BI5 Tick authority and source-native M15 reconstruction
Source-native event detection and first-Tick Bid/Ask executable chronology
First-binding-failure stop before protected periods, Core/MT4 or 2025
retained_findings: A completely Dukascopy-native construction retained positive pooled economics at +¥17,005 and PF 1.110.
The pooled result was not portable across all folds or months; 2024H2 was negative and only 13/24 months were positive.
The positive result was concentrated directionally in Short while Long was slightly negative.
Diagnostic realized-close portfolio replay added net and reduced realized DD but worsened 5-day and 20-day loss clusters.
falsified_or_unsupported_claims: The fixed all-Dukascopy Pullback Continuation candidate is portable across all four development folds.
The fixed candidate has balanced Long and Short alpha.
The candidate may proceed to concentration, historical validation, Core/MT4 or 2025 gates.
prohibited_reuse: EMA, ATR, pullback tolerance or hold-time retuning
2020-2022 or 2025 outcome access for HYP-036 rescue
entries.exact_next_action: Close HYP-036 at the standalone portability gate; do not rescue the observed Short/session/period pattern.
